name: NY-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+32 partisan lean makes a Republican win highly improbable
Open seat after Espaillat lost renomination, but Democratic nominee is heavily favored
Avila Chevalier raised $1.35M with substantial outside support; Republican candidate has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The D+32 baseline and fundamentals point to a lopsided Democratic hold, and the market consensus plus the Republican's negligible campaign infrastructure confirm it. The open-seat wrinkle and lack of polling add modest uncertainty but not enough to move the race out of Safe D.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or primary-faction backlash against the Democratic nominee could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Adriano Espaillat (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This Upper Manhattan district is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+32. Adriano Espaillat is not on the ballot after losing renomination, so Democrats will run Darializa Avila Chevalier, who enters the general with a strong fundraising record and significant outside spending on her behalf. Republican Jomo Williams has no reported fundraising or outside support.

With no public polling or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win near 97%. The expected margin is roughly 30 points, consistent with the baseline model, and the seat remains safely in Democratic hands.
